title: REGULATIONS ON THE PERSONNEL MANAGEMENT OF PUBLIC OFFICIALS IN PROFESSIONAL SERVICE
full_text:
CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose) The purpose of this Decree is to prescribe special cases regarding the classification of ranks, appointment, performance evaluation, etc. of public officials in professional functional groups and categories, with rank classifications distinct from those of public officials in general service under Article 4(2) of the State Public Officials Act and Article 3(2) of the Decree on the Appointment of Public Officials.

Article 2 (Scope of application) (1) This Decree shall apply to public officials whose personnel management and transfer are restricted to certain specialized areas, and who fall under each functional category in Appendix 1 (hereinafter referred to as "public officials in professional service").
  (2) Except as provided in this Decree, the Decree on the Appointment of Public Officials (hereinafter referred to as the "Appointment Decree") shall apply to the appointment of public officials in professional service; provided, Articles 4, 5, 22-3, 29(1) and (2), 30, 31(1), 33, 35, 35-5, and 45 of the Appointment Decree shall not apply. <Amended on Jul. 27, 2021; Jul. 7, 2025>
  (3) Except as provided in this Decree, the Regulations on the Performance Evaluation of Public Officials (hereinafter referred to as the "Regulations on the Performance Evaluation") shall apply to the performance evaluation of public officials in professional service; provided, Articles 7-2, 10, 14, 16, 23 through 27, 29, and 30 of the Regulations on the Performance Evaluation shall not apply. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (4) Except as provided in this Decree, the Decree on Public Officials Appointment Examinations (hereinafter referred to as the "Examination Decree") shall apply to appointment examinations for public officials in professional service; provided, Articles 23-2 through 23-4 and 37 through 46 of the Examination Decree shall not apply. <Added on Jul. 27, 2021>

Article 3 (Classification of ranks) (1) The ranks of public officials in professional service shall be classified into senior professional official, professional official, and associate professional official. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (2) The names of functional groups, categories, subcategories, and classes of public officials in professional service shall be as specified in Appendix 1.
  (3) A senior professional official shall be equivalent to Grade III or IV in general service, a professional official to Grade V in general service, and an associate professional official to Grade VI in general service. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (4) The competent Minister shall determine the ranks of public officials in professional service in accordance with any of the following classifications and, where he or she intends to change such classification, shall consult with the Minister of Personnel Management: <Added on Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. Senior professional officials and professional officials; 
  2. Senior professional officials, professional officials, and associate professional officials;
  3. Professional officials and associate professional officials.

Article 4 (Scope of appointment authority) (1) Senior professional officials and professional officials shall be appointed by the President, upon the recommendation of the competent Minister, after consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management and through the Prime Minister; and associate professional officials shall be appointed by the competent Minister. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (2) Pursuant to Article 32(3) of the State Public Officials Act (hereinafter referred to as the “Act”), the President shall delegate his or her authority to appoint public officials in professional service to the competent Minister, except the authority to promote a senior professional official to a position in the Senior Executive Service. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (3) The competent Minister may delegate the authority to transfer senior professional officials and professional officials and the authority to appoint associate professional officials to the head of an agency under his or her jurisdiction, if the agency is headed by a public official who is a member of the Senior Executive Service (hereinafter referred to as “high-ranking public official”) or by a higher-ranking public official. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (4) The competent Minister or a person to whom appointment authority has been delegated pursuant to paragraph (3) may, with the approval of the delegating authority, delegate to the head of an agency under his or her jurisdiction the authority to appoint associate professional officials of that agency if the agency is headed by a public official of Grade IV or higher or by a high-ranking public official, and the authority to transfer associate professional officials of that agency if the agency is headed by a public official of Grade V. <Added on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (5) Notwithstanding paragraphs (2) through (4), the competent Minister or the head of the relevant superior agency may exercise appointment authority according to the following classifications: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. Appointment following an adjustment in the fixed number of personnel: The competent Minister;
  2. Personnel exchanges between competent Ministers: The competent Minister;
  3. Personnel exchanges between affiliated agencies: The competent Minister or the head of the relevant superior agency;
  4. Personnel exchanges between auxiliary agencies: The competent Minister;
  5. Personnel exchanges between auxiliary agencies and affiliated agencies: The competent Minister.

CHAPTER II DESIGNATION OF SPECIALIZED FIELDS

Article 5 (Designation of specialized fields) (1) The competent Minister may, in consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management, designate as specialized fields those fields under his or her jurisdiction that involve duties unique to the relevant ministry and require the accumulation of expertise and long-term service. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (2) When intending to designate a specialized field that involves affairs performed by multiple institutions with different jurisdictions, the relevant Ministers may jointly designate such field in consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (3) In any of the following cases, the competent Minister may change or cancel the designation of specialized fields in consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management:
  1. Large-scale organizational and functional restructuring, or changes to the fixed number of personnel;
  2. Increased need to change or cancel the designation of specialized fields due to rapid internal and external environmental changes.
  (4) If the competent Minister designates a specialized field pursuant to paragraph (1) or (2) or changes it pursuant to paragraph (3), he or she shall prepare a pathway for assigning positions for public officials in professional service.
  (5) In consulting on the cancellation of the designation of specialized fields pursuant to paragraph (3), he or she shall consult with the Minister of the Interior and Safety regarding matters related to the organization, such as changes in the organization and the fixed number of personnel, <Amended on Jul. 26, 2017>
  (6) When canceling the designation of specialized fields pursuant to paragraph (3), the competent Minister shall reassign a public official in professional service according to the following classifications:
  1. Where a public official in general service who is not in professional service is reassigned to a position as a public official in professional service: He or she shall be reassigned to a functional group or category in which he or she has previously served;
  2. Where a public official is newly employed through an open competitive examination, etc.: He or she shall be reassigned to a functional group or category in which the continuity of his or her duties is recognized, in consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), details necessary for the designation and operation of specialized fields shall be determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.

CHAPTER III NEW EMPLOYMENT AND REASSIGNMENT

Article 6 (Requirements for competitive recruitment for career service positions) (1) A person employed as a public official in professional service pursuant to the main clause or the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 28(2) of the Act shall meet the requirements prescribed in subparagraphs 1, 2, 3, 7, 8, 10, and 13 of that paragraph and the requirements prescribed in Article 16 of the Appointment Decree. In such cases, a person eligible to apply for a competitive recruitment examination, etc. for career service positions for public officials in professional service (referring to a recruitment examination under the main clause or the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 28(2) of the Act; hereafter in this Article the same shall apply) pursuant to Article 16(1)2, 3, or 10 of the Appointment Decree shall meet the requirements prescribed in paragraph (2).
  (2) A person who intends to apply for a competitive recruitment examination, etc. for career service positions for public officials in professional service under Article 16(1)2 or 3 of the Appointment Decree under the latter part of paragraph (1) shall meet the qualifications for application under Article 27 of the Examination Decree, and a person who intends to apply for a competitive recruitment examination, etc. for career service positions for public officials in professional service under Article 16(1)10 of the Appointment Decree shall hold a doctorate or master's degree in the relevant field of duties, and shall meet the criteria for the required career years for each rank to be appointed as specified in Appendix 2.
  (3) If the functional groups and categories specified in Appendices 1, 5, or 8 of the Examination Decree are applied to the employment of public officials in professional service pursuant to the main clause or the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 28 (2) of the Act, the functional groups and categories shall be deemed those of public officials in professional service.
  [This Article Wholly Amended on Jul. 27, 2021]

Article 6-2 (Probationary appointment and exemption therefrom) (1) A professional official newly recruited shall be appointed on a probationary basis for 1 year and an associate professional official newly recruited shall be appointed on a probationary basis for 6 months, and each shall be appointed as a regular public official in consideration of his or her work performance, performance in education and training, qualities as a public official, etc. during the relevant probationary period. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (2) When applying Article 25 of the Appointment Decree with respect to an exemption from probationary appointment or a reduction of a probationary appointment period for professional officials and associate professional officials, “the minimum number of years required for promotion under Article 31” in Article 25(2)1 of that Decree shall be construed as “the minimum number of years required for promotion under Article 10 of the Regulations on the Personnel Management of Public Officials in Professional Service”. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  [This Article Added on Jul. 27, 2021]

Article 7 (Reassignment) (1) In any of the following cases, an appointing authority may reassign a public official in general service not in professional service as a public official in professional service or vice versa: <Amended Jul. 27, 2021; Dec. 26, 2023; Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. Where a public official in general service of Grade VII or higher specified in Appendix 1 of the Appointment Decree intends to be reassigned to a professional job series; in such cases, the relevant period specified in the following items (excluding any period of leave of absence, release from position, or suspension from office) shall have elapsed:
  a. Public officials of Grade V: A period of at least 1 year determined by the competent Minister from the date of initial appointment to the relevant rank; provided, for a person who has served as a public official of Grade VI for at least 3 years, such period may be shortened based on his or her length of service;
  b. Public officials of Grade VI or VII: A period of at least 3 years determined by the competent Minister from the date of initial appointment to Grade VI or VII.
  2. Where adjustment in the number of personnel in the relevant position is necessary due to changes or abolition of organizations, or changes to or elimination of the fixed number of personnel;
  3. Where the designation of specialized fields is canceled pursuant to Article 5(3).
  4. Where the competent Minister has consulted with the Minister of Personnel Management because it is particularly necessary to utilize public officials in professional service in a field other than a specialized field to perform a national project or duties assisting the competent Minister, etc.;
  5. Where a public official in professional service is reassigned as a public official in general service following a resolution by the Appointment Review Committee under Article 8.
  (2) If a public official in general service of Grade VII or higher who has been hired through a recruitment examination under the main clause and the proviso, with the exception of the subparagraphs, of Article 28(2) of the Act intends to be reassigned as a public official in professional service in his or her specialized field (as referred to in Article 5), the period of restriction on reassignment under Article 29(3) of the Appointment Decree shall not apply. <Added on Jul. 27, 2021; Jun. 30, 2026>
  (3) A public official in professional service shall not be reassigned to a job series outside the professional job family for 7 years, or to another job series within the professional job family for 5 years, from the date of his or her initial appointment as a public official in professional service; provided, he or she may be reassigned in cases falling under paragraph (1)2 through 5. <Amended on Jul. 27, 2021; Jun. 30, 2026>
  (4) In calculating the period of restriction on reassignment under paragraph (3), the periods specified in the following subparagraphs shall be included, but any period of leave of absence, release from position, or suspension from office shall not be included: <Amended on Jul. 27, 2021; Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. A period during which a public official in professional service served on a probationary basis;
  2. A period during which a public official in professional service previously served as such, where the public official, after being reassigned as a public official in general service in a case falling under paragraph (1)4, is reassigned as a public official in professional service within 2 years from the date of reassignment to general service;
  3. A period, not exceeding 3 years, during which a specialist appointed to a specialist position under Article 43-3(3) of the Appointment Decree served in such position, where he or she is reassigned as a public official in professional service in the same specialized field (limited to the position held at the time of such reassignment).
  (5) When reassigning public officials in professional service to a job series, outside of a professional job family or reassigning public officials in general service falling under a job series outside of the professional job family as public officials in professional service, the appointing authority shall determine the class or position of the person to be appointed based on the standards established by the Minister of Personnel Management. <Amended on Jul. 27, 2021>

Article 8 (Order for reassignment) (1) Where a public official in professional service is unsuitable for performing duties in a specialized field because he or she falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the appointing authority may reassign the public official according to the classifications specified in the subparagraphs of Article 5(6); in such cases, the reassignment shall be subject to a resolution by the Appointment Review Committee under Article 10-4 of the Appointment Decree (hereinafter referred to as the “Appointment Review Committee”):
  1. Where misconduct related to the public official’s duties or misconduct committed by taking advantage of his or her position, etc. falls under any of the following items:
  a. Where disciplinary action or a disciplinary resolution has been requested against the public official (including a request for review or re-review under Article 82(2) of the Act), or where the public official is within a period of restriction on promotion following disciplinary action;
  b. Where an investigation or inquiry is underway after the public official receives notice of the commencement of an investigation or inquiry under Article 83(3) of the Act or notice of the commencement of an investigation under Article 24(1) of the Act on Public Sector Audits;
  2. Where the public official receives the lowest grade in a work performance evaluation under Article 14(1) or 14-2(1), or in an expertise evaluation under Article 14(1)2 or 14-2(1)2.
  (2) Before determining whether to reassign a public official pursuant to paragraph (1), the appointing authority shall notify the relevant public official in writing of the reasons and grounds for finding him or her unsuitable for performing duties in a specialized field and shall provide him or her with an opportunity to submit an opinion to the Appointment Review Committee.
  (3) When reviewing whether to reassign a public official pursuant to paragraph (1), the Appointment Review Committee may resolve to defer reassignment if improvement in the expertise and competence of a public official in professional service falling under paragraph (1)2 is expected.
  (4) The appointing authority shall submit to the Appointment Review Committee the results of the first work performance evaluation conducted for a person subject to a resolution to defer reassignment after the date on which 3 months have elapsed since the resolution was adopted under paragraph (3), and the Appointment Review Committee shall resolve whether to reassign the person.
  (5) If necessary for its review, the Appointment Review Committee may have relevant experts attend its meetings to hear their opinions.
  (6) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (5), details necessary for the procedures for and operation of orders for reassignment shall be determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

Article 9 (Examination for reassignment) (1) The examination for reassignment as a public official in professional service shall consist of document screening and an oral interview, but if necessary, an additional written or practical examination may also be conducted.
  (2) In cases falling under paragraph (1), if the number of applicants is at least 3 times the number of persons to be selected, the competent Minister may select at least 3 times the number of people to be selected through document screening based on the criteria appropriate to the duties of the position to be filled, and then proceed to oral interviews, etc.
  (3) The competent Minister shall appoint or commission any of the following persons as examiners to prepare and score the examinations for reassignment under paragraph (1) and to take charge of other matters necessary for conducting the examinations: <Added on Dec. 26, 2023>
  1. Persons of a higher rank than the class to which the reassignment is planned (including public officials corresponding to the higher rank);
  2. Persons who are not public officials (excluding faculty members of national or public universities) with abundant experience and knowledge in the fields related to the duties for which reassignment is to be made.
  (4) The examination committee shall consist of at least 3 but not more than 5 members in consideration of gender diversity, and a majority of the committee members shall be those falling under paragraph (3)2. <Added on Dec. 26, 2023>
  (5) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (4), matters necessary for administering examinations for reassignment shall be determined by the Minister of Personnel Management. <Added on Dec. 26, 2023>

Article 9-2 (Exemption from examination for reassignment) The appointing authority may reassign a public official without an examination for reassignment in any of the following cases:
  1. Where the public official is reassigned to a job series in which he or she previously served (limited to cases where his or her status as a public official has remained uninterrupted);
  2. Among cases of reassignment under Article 7(1)2, where only the title of the grade is changed within the same job family without any change in job duties.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

CHAPTER IV PROMOTION

Article 10 (Minimum number of years required for promotion) (1) To be promoted, a public official in professional service shall have served in the relevant rank or an equivalent rank for the period specified in the following subparagraphs: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. Professional officials: At least 3 years (a person reassigned pursuant to Article 7(1)1 shall have served as a professional official for at least 1 year);
  2. Associate professional officials: At least 2 years (a person reassigned pursuant to Article 7(1)1 shall have served as an associate professional official for at least 6 months).
  (2) In calculating the period of service under paragraph (1), periods of service as a public official in general service specified in the following subparagraphs shall be counted at 100 percent: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. For professional officials, the following periods of service:
  a. A period of service in a rank equivalent to Grade V or higher;
  b. A period of service as a local public official equivalent to Grade V or higher;
  2. For associate professional officials, the following periods of service:
  a. A period of service in a rank equivalent to Grade VI or higher;
  b. A period of service as a local public official equivalent to Grade VI or higher.

Article 11 (Promotion to senior professional official or professional official) The promotion of a professional official to senior professional official or of an associate professional official to professional official shall be made from among persons included in the list of candidates for promotion of the relevant agency following screening for promotion by an ordinary promotion screening committee under Article 40-3(2) of the Act. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  [Title Amended on Jun. 30, 2026]

Article 11-2 (Promotion to public official of Grade IV) Where the classification of ranks of public officials in professional service falls under Article 3(4)3, the appointing authority may promote a professional official to a public official of Grade IV according to the following classifications after screening for promotion by an ordinary promotion screening committee under Article 40-3(2) of the Act:
  1. Where a public official in general service who is not a public official in professional service has been reassigned as a public official in professional service: A public official of Grade IV in the job family and job series in which he or she previously served;
  2. Where a person has been newly recruited through an open competitive recruitment examination, etc.: A public official of Grade IV in a job family and job series in which continuity of duties is recognized in consultation with the Minister of Personnel Management.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

CHAPTER V PERSONAL MANAGEMENT, SUCH AS RESTRICTION ON TRANSFER

Article 12 (Standards for personnel management) The competent Minister shall establish and implement the standards for the management of assignment, reassignment, transfer, promotion, etc. of public officials in professional service under his or her jurisdiction, as prescribed in Article 32-5 of the Act, the Appointment Decree, and this Decree.

Article 13 (Restriction on transfer) (1) The appointing authority or the appointment-recommendation authority shall not transfer public officials in professional service under his or her jurisdiction to a field outside their specialized fields or to another specialized field.
  (2) The appointing authority or the appointment-recommendation authority may transfer a public official in professional service under his or her jurisdiction to another position only after the compulsory service period in a position has expired, and this period, which shall be 1 year, begins from the date of his or her appointment to the position.

CHAPTER VI PERFORMANCE EVALUATION

Article 14 (Evaluation of performance-based contracting) (1) The work performance evaluation of senior professional officials and professional officials shall be based on the following evaluation criteria (hereinafter referred to as "evaluation of performance-based contracting, etc."):
  1. Level of achievement of performance goals;
  2. Results of evaluation of expertise or ability related to the performance of duties (hereinafter referred to as "expertise evaluation");
  3. Results of operation evaluations by department (limited to cases deemed necessary by the Minister).
  (2) The achievement level of performance goals under paragraph (1)1 shall be evaluated based on evaluation indicators, such as the results, etc. of implementing performance goals achieved by the public officials subject to evaluation during the evaluation period. In such cases, the evaluation may be conducted in consideration of the importance, difficulty, etc. of performance objectives.
  (3) Expertise evaluation shall be conducted in consideration of the professional knowledge, skills, ability to perform duties, experience in the specialized field, etc. of public officials, and specific evaluation elements shall be determined by the competent Minister.
  (4) The evaluation of performance-based contracting, etc. shall include at least 3 grades, and the lowest grade may be granted to a public official who meets the requirements determined by the Minister, such as misconduct during duty performance.
  (5) The competent Minister shall determine matters necessary for the requirements for assigning the lowest grade to public officials pursuant to paragraph (4) and specific procedures, etc. in consideration of the standards and scope set by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (6) The competent Minister shall award points to senior professional officials and professional officials according to grades for the evaluation of performance-based contracting, etc. based on standards determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (7) The competent Minister shall convert the previous work performance ratings of public officials at equivalent ranks before their reassignment as public officials in professional service into points for each grade in the evaluation of performance-based contracting, as determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.

Article 14-2 (Work performance evaluation) (1) The work performance rating of associate professional officials shall be based on an evaluation of the following items (hereinafter referred to as “work performance evaluation”):
  1. Work performance;
  2. Evaluation of expertise;
  3. Attitude toward performing duties or the results of an evaluation of department-level operations (limited to cases where the competent Minister deems it necessary).
  (2) Evaluation components for each evaluation item under paragraph (1) shall be determined by the competent Minister, reflecting the characteristics of duties by grade, department, or specialized field. In such cases, the evaluation components shall be determined to ensure that they are relevant to the duties performed by the public officials subject to evaluation and that the work performance evaluations are conducted objectively.
  (3) Work performance evaluations shall be conducted for each evaluation unit organized by grade; provided, the competent Minister may determine the evaluation units differently in consideration of the similarity of duties, the number of public officials in each grade, etc.
  (4) The evaluation of expertise shall be conducted in consideration of a public official’s professional knowledge and skills, competence in performing duties, experience in a specialized field, etc., and specific evaluation components shall be determined by the competent Minister.
  (5) An evaluator for a work performance evaluation shall conduct the evaluation in consideration of the extent to which a public official subject to evaluation has achieved his or her performance goals, etc., and may assign the lowest grade to a public official who satisfies any of the criteria determined by the competent Minister, including the commission of misconduct in the course of duties.
  (6) The competent Minister shall determine matters necessary for the requirements for assigning the lowest grade to a public official under paragraph (5), detailed procedures for assigning such grade, etc., taking into account the standards and scope determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (7) There shall be at least 3 evaluation grades, and evaluations shall be conducted so that the highest grade is assigned to the top 20 percent and the lowest grade to the bottom 10 percent of the public officials in each evaluation unit; provided, where the competent Minister deems it necessary, he or she may set a different distribution ratio for the highest or lowest grade.
  (8) Evaluators and confirmers of work performance evaluations shall submit the results of such evaluations to the Work Performance Evaluation Committee under Article 14-4.
  (9) The competent Minister shall convert the results of work performance ratings received while serving in an equivalent rank before reassignment as a public official in professional service into scores corresponding to the respective evaluation grades and assign such scores, as determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

Article 14-3 (Exceptions to work performance evaluations) (1) Where a work performance evaluation of an associate professional official cannot be conducted pursuant to Article 17(1) of the Regulations on the Performance Evaluation, the average of the results of his or her 2 most recent work performance evaluations shall be deemed his or her evaluation result; provided, where no work performance evaluation has previously been conducted for the public official, the evaluation result shall be 60 percent of the full score.
  (2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), Article 17(1) through (3) and (5) of the Regulations on the Performance Evaluation shall apply to exceptions to work performance evaluations.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

Article 14-4 (Work Performance Evaluation Committee) (1) The Work Performance Evaluation Committee shall assign work performance evaluation scores by grade to public officials subject to evaluation based on the results of work performance evaluations submitted by each evaluation unit. In such cases, work performance evaluation scores mean the scores for each evaluation grade determined by the competent Minister in accordance with the standards determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (2) Except as provided in paragraph (1), Article 18(1) through (3) and (5) through (7) of the Regulations on the Performance Evaluation shall apply to matters relating to the Work Performance Evaluation Committee.
  [This Article Added on Jun. 30, 2026]

Article 15 (Service year ratings) (1) The years of service of professional officials and associate professional officials who have completed the minimum number of years required for promotion under Article 10(1) as of the applicable reference date specified in the following subparagraphs shall be rated, and the ratings shall be reflected in promotion: <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. Professional officials: December 31;
  2. Associate professional officials: June 30 and December 31 (hereinafter referred to as “regular rating reference dates”); provided, where the competent Minister deems it necessary, he or she may set different regular rating reference dates, but shall ensure that the rating period remains unchanged, and may conduct the rating once a year.
  (2) Persons in charge of personnel affairs in each agency shall be responsible for verifying service year ratings; provided, the competent Minister may designate a different verifier, if particularly necessary.
  (3) As of the applicable reference date specified in the subparagraphs of paragraph (1), a service year rating shall cover the period during which a public official subject to the rating has actually performed duties at the relevant rank or higher, or at an equivalent rank or higher. <Amended on Dec. 26, 2023; Jun. 30, 2026>
  (4) In cases falling under paragraph (3), the periods of leave of absence, release from position, disciplinary disposition, and restriction on promotion under Article 32 of the Appointment Decree shall not be included; provided, the periods of leave of absence and release from position, which are included in the minimum number of years required for promotion pursuant to Article 31 of the Appointment Decree, shall be deemed the period during which he or she has been engaged in his or her duties in the class or rank held at the time of the leave of absence or release from position and rated accordingly.
  (5) Matters necessary for the method of calculating service year ratings such as equivalent ranks between the service years of public officials of different service categories or between the service years of public officials and service years in the private sector, the conversion rate of service years, and the number of service years shall be determined by the Minister of Personnel Management and Innovation.

Article 16 (Additional point ratings) (1) The competent Minister may award up to 5 additional points in consideration of his or her work experience in specific positions or special areas, achievements such as work innovations during the period subject to work performance evaluation, and other job characteristics and contribution.
  (2) The standards, etc. for granting additional points under paragraph (1) shall be determined by the competent Minister in consideration of the items, scope, etc. determined by the Minister of Personnel Management.
  (3) When intending to change the standards for granting additional points under paragraph (2), the competent Minister shall disclose in advance the details of such change to public officials under his or her jurisdiction to gather opinions from them prior to the work performance evaluation period.

Article 17 (Preparation of lists of candidates for promotion) (1) Work performance rating scores assigned pursuant to Articles 14(6) and 14-4(1) shall be accumulated for at least the number of years determined by the competent Minister in accordance with the standards determined by the Minister of Personnel Management, taking into account the average number of years required for promotion by agency, etc. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (2) Scores awarded for service year ratings pursuant to Article 15 shall be accumulated over at least the number of years determined by the competent Minister taking into account the average number of years required for promotion, etc. by institution in accordance with the standards determined by the Minister of Personnel Management and Innovation.
  (3) As of January 31 for professional officials and as of January 31 and July 31 for associate professional officials, the appointing authority shall prepare lists of candidates for promotion, separately by specialized field and by grade to which promotion is expected, for professional officials and associate professional officials who meet all the criteria specified in the following subparagraphs; provided, where different reference dates for regular evaluations and regular ratings have been set for associate professional officials, the lists of candidates for promotion shall be prepared as of the last day of the month following each relevant reference date: <Amended on Dec. 27, 2022; Jun. 30, 2026>
  1. The cumulative score by grade under paragraph (1) shall be at least 95 points;
  2. The cumulative score for service year ratings under paragraph (2) shall be at least 5 points.
  (4) The total rating score on a list of candidates for promotion shall be the sum of the cumulative scores for each evaluation grade under paragraph (1), the cumulative scores from ratings of years of service under paragraph (2), and, for a person eligible for additional points under Article 16, such additional points. <Amended on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (5) If deemed necessary, the appointing authority may prepare a lists of candidates for promotion by consolidating functional categories with similar duties which maintain an appropriate balance in terms of the number of candidates. In such cases, any changes made shall apply after 1 year from the date of the change.
  (6) A list of candidates for promotion shall take effect on the day following the applicable reference date for its preparation under paragraph (3); provided, where the list is adjusted or entries are deleted therefrom, the list as adjusted shall take effect on the following day. <Added on Jun. 30, 2026>
  (7) Except as provided in paragraphs (1) through (6), matters necessary for the methods of calculating work performance evaluation scores to be reflected in a list of candidates for promotion, determining the rankings of persons with the same total rating score on the list, adjusting the list or deleting entries therefrom, disclosing the rankings on the list, etc. shall be determined by the Minister of Personnel Management. <Added on Jun. 30, 2026>

ADDENDA <Presidential Decree No. 27787, Jan. 10, 2017>
Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force 1 month after the date of its promulgation.
Article 2 (Special cases concerning period of restriction on reassignment)
Notwithstanding the main clause of Article 7(2), the period of restriction on reassignment for those who were reassigned as public officials in professional service pursuant to Article 7(1) in 2017 shall be 4 years for reassignment to a functional category outside a professional functional group, and 3 years for reassignment to another functional category within the professional functional group.
Article 3 Omitted.

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on the date of its promulgation; provided, among the Presidential decrees amended under Article 8 of the Addenda, the amendments to a Presidential Decree, which was promulgated before this Decree enters into force but the date it enters into force has yet to arrive, shall enter into force on the enforcement date of the relevant Presidential Decree.

Article 1 (Enforcement date)

Article 2 (Applicability to compulsory service period in a position)
The amended provisions of the proviso of Article 2(2) shall also apply to public officials in professional service who are in office as at the time this Decree enters into force. In such cases, the compulsory service period in a position shall be counted from the date of his or her appointment to the position held as at the time this Decree enters into force.
Article 3 (Transitional measures concerning reorganization of function subcategories of public officials in professional service)
(1) Public officials in professional service in the functional subcategories specified in the left column of the following table specified in the previous Appendix 1 as at the time this Decree enters into force shall be deemed appointed to the relevant class in the functional subcategories indicated in the right column of the following table under the amended provisions of Appendix 1.
(2) If procedures for the recruitment and appointment of public officials in professional service in the functional subcategories specified in the left column of Appendix provided in paragraph (1) are ongoing as at the time this Decree enters into force, the procedures in the functional subcategories specified in the right column of that Table shall be deemed ongoing.
(3) Any other statutes or regulations that refer to the classes of public officials in professional service in the functional subcategories listed in the left column of Appendix in paragraph (1) as at the time this Decree enters into force, shall be deemed refer to the relevant classes in the functional subcategories listed in the right column of that Table.
